title: Biological Molecules Summary
content:
# Biological Molecules Summary

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Review and compare all major biological molecules
- Link structure to function for each molecule type
- Understand the importance of biological molecules in living organisms
- Apply knowledge to exam-style questions

## Introduction

This lesson summarises the key concepts about biological molecules. Understanding how carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids are structured, and how this relates to their functions, is fundamental to understanding life at the molecular level.

## Key Concepts

### Overview of Biological Molecules

| Molecule type | Elements | Monomers | Functions |
|---------------|----------|----------|----------|
| Carbohydrates | C, H, O | Monosaccharides | Energy, storage, structure |
| Lipids | C, H, O | Not polymers | Energy storage, membranes, insulation |
| Proteins | C, H, O, N (S) | Amino acids | Enzymes, structure, transport, defence |
| Nucleic acids | C, H, O, N, P | Nucleotides | Genetic information |

### Carbohydrates Summary

**Classification:**

| Type | Examples | Function |
|------|----------|----------|
| Monosaccharides | Glucose, fructose | Quick energy, building blocks |
| Disaccharides | Sucrose, maltose, lactose | Transport, energy |
| Polysaccharides | Starch, glycogen, cellulose | Storage, structure |

**Key reactions:**
- Condensation: monosaccharides → polysaccharides + water
- Hydrolysis: polysaccharides + water → monosaccharides
- Bond: Glycosidic bond

**Structure-function:**
| Polysaccharide | Structure feature | Function enabled |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Starch (amylose) | Helical, compact | Efficient storage |
| Starch (amylopectin) | Branched | Rapid hydrolysis |
| Glycogen | Highly branched | Very rapid energy release |
| Cellulose | Straight chains, H-bonds | Structural strength |

### Lipids Summary

**Types:**

| Type | Components | Function |
|------|------------|----------|
| Triglycerides | Glycerol + 3 fatty acids | Energy storage |
| Phospholipids | Glycerol + 2 FA + phosphate | Membranes |

**Key reactions:**
- Condensation: glycerol + fatty acids → triglyceride + water
- Bond: Ester bond

**Structure-function:**
| Feature | Function |
|---------|----------|
| High H:O ratio | High energy per gram |
| Insoluble | Doesn't affect water potential |
| Hydrophobic tails | Form membrane bilayers |
| Amphipathic (phospholipids) | Self-assemble into membranes |

### Proteins Summary

**Levels of structure:**

| Level | Description | Bonds |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| Primary | Amino acid sequence | Peptide bonds |
| Secondary | α-helix, β-sheet | Hydrogen bonds |
| Tertiary | Overall 3D shape | Multiple bond types |
| Quaternary | Multiple polypeptides | Same as tertiary |

**Key reactions:**
- Condensation: amino acids → polypeptide + water
- Bond: Peptide bond

**Diversity of functions:**
| Function | Example |
|----------|----------|
| Catalysis | Enzymes (amylase) |
| Structure | Collagen, keratin |
| Transport | Haemoglobin |
| Defence | Antibodies |
| Hormones | Insulin |
| Contraction | Actin, myosin |

### Enzymes Summary

**Key concepts:**
- Biological catalysts
- Lower activation energy
- Specific to substrates (active site)
- Affected by temperature, pH, concentration
- Induced fit model

**Inhibition:**
| Type | Binding site | Effect of ↑[S] |
|------|--------------|----------------|
| Competitive | Active site | Reduces inhibition |
| Non-competitive | Allosteric site | No effect |

### Condensation and Hydrolysis

**Universal reactions:**

| Reaction | What happens | When |
|----------|--------------|------|
| Condensation | Monomers join, water released | Building molecules |
| Hydrolysis | Water added, polymer split | Breaking down molecules |

**Bond types:**
| Bond | Forms between | Found in |
|------|---------------|----------|
| Glycosidic | Sugars | Carbohydrates |
| Peptide | Amino acids | Proteins |
| Ester | Glycerol + fatty acids | Lipids |

### Food Tests Summary

| Test | For | Positive result |
|------|-----|------------------|
| Benedict's (heat) | Reducing sugars | Blue → orange/red |
| Benedict's + HCl | Non-reducing sugars | Blue → orange/red after hydrolysis |
| Iodine | Starch | Brown → blue-black |
| Biuret | Proteins | Blue → purple |
| Emulsion | Lipids | Cloudy white |

### Comparing Molecules

| Property | Carbohydrates | Lipids | Proteins |
|----------|---------------|--------|----------|
| Elements | C, H, O | C, H, O | C, H, O, N |
| Monomer | Monosaccharide | N/A | Amino acid |
| Bond | Glycosidic | Ester | Peptide |
| Solubility | Varies | Insoluble | Varies |
| Energy (kJ/g) | ~16 | ~39 | ~17 |

### Common Calculations

**Energy from respiration:**
$$\text{Energy} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Energy per gram}$$

**Percentage calculations:**
$$\%\text{ nutrient} = \frac{\text{Mass of nutrient}}{\text{Total mass}} \times 100$$

### Linking to Other Topics

| Topic | Connection |
|-------|------------|
| Cells | Membranes (phospholipids), cytoplasm (proteins) |
| Nutrition | Digestion breaks down molecules |
| Transport | Proteins in blood, glucose transport |
| Respiration | Glucose as substrate |
| DNA | Nucleic acids carry genetic code |
| Enzymes | Control all metabolic reactions |

### Key Diagrams to Know

| Molecule | What to draw |
|----------|---------------|
| Amino acid | General structure with R group |
| Peptide bond | Formation between amino acids |
| Glucose | Ring structure (α and β) |
| Triglyceride | Glycerol + 3 fatty acids |
| Phospholipid | Head and tails |

## Common Exam Questions

- Compare the structure and function of starch and cellulose
- Explain how protein structure relates to function
- Describe the tests for biological molecules
- Explain condensation and hydrolysis reactions

## Common Misconceptions Review

| Misconception | Reality |
|--------------|---------|
| Lipids are polymers | Lipids are NOT polymers |
| All sugars reduce Benedict's | Only reducing sugars |
| Proteins only function as enzymes | Proteins have many functions |
| Primary structure includes H-bonds | Only peptide bonds |
| All carbohydrates are sweet | Polysaccharides are not sweet |
| Denaturation breaks peptide bonds | Only shape changes |

## Practice Questions

1. State the elements found in proteins but not in carbohydrates. (1 mark)

2. Name the bond formed between amino acids and describe how it forms. (3 marks)

3. Compare starch and cellulose in terms of their structure and function. (4 marks)

4. Explain why lipids store more energy per gram than carbohydrates. (2 marks)

5. Describe the tests you would use to identify the presence of a reducing sugar and a protein in a food sample. (4 marks)

6. Discuss the relationship between structure and function in biological molecules, using named examples of carbohydrates and proteins. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Review

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Monomer | Small molecule that joins to form polymers |
| Polymer | Large molecule made of repeating monomers |
| Condensation | Reaction joining molecules, releasing water |
| Hydrolysis | Reaction splitting molecules using water |
| Glycosidic bond | Bond between sugars |
| Peptide bond | Bond between amino acids |
| Ester bond | Bond in lipids |
| Denaturation | Loss of protein shape and function |
| Active site | Region of enzyme where substrate binds |

## Summary

- **Carbohydrates:** C, H, O; monosaccharides → polysaccharides; energy and structure
- **Lipids:** C, H, O; glycerol + fatty acids; energy storage and membranes
- **Proteins:** C, H, O, N; amino acids → polypeptides; diverse functions
- **Condensation** joins monomers (releases water)
- **Hydrolysis** breaks polymers (uses water)
- Structure determines function at all levels
- Enzymes are protein catalysts with specific shapes
- Food tests identify molecules by colour changes
- Understanding biological molecules is fundamental to biology
